meta_description:
813 likes, 22 comments - aliabdaal on October 15, 2026: "At 21, I was making around £3,000 a month in profit while studying medicine full-time.

I’d combined three things I was already good at: teaching, building websites and the BMAT medical-school entrance exam.

So I created a course to help other students prepare for it.

For the first few years, I did almost everything myself.

Then one weekend, I couldn’t teach, so I asked if my two friends wanted to run the course without me and get paid for it. Of course they said yes. 

The feedback was just as good as it was when it was just me running it. 

That was a huge unlock for me when I realised the business didn’t need me to deliver every part of it.

Delegating helped me scale my time, but I also accidentally outsourced the part I enjoyed most.

So, two lessons:

1️⃣ You don’t need to do everything yourself.

2️⃣ Be careful not to delegate the work you actually love.

After all, what’s the point of running a business if you’re not having fun?

Follow @aliabdaal for more stories like this :) 

And if you want my free 7-lesson course on how to build a strong $100k a year business with the skills you already have, comment FOUNDATIONS below and I’ll send it your way.".
